title: Segregation of duties in finance
context: At GlobalConnect Manila the finance team of three keeps the supplier master and approves supplier payments in the finance system. LedgerSim is a brand-neutral simulator that shows the same governance information: users and roles, the supplier master change log and payments. All amounts are in PHP. All finance data is synthetic.
atWork: At work, a junior analyst reads the finance system itself when a segregation-of-duties finding needs evidence: who holds which roles, what the account did, and whether anyone looked.
owner: Your walk-through found that one of the finance team both creates suppliers and approves their payments. Before the control sprint closes, look at the finance system as it is today and capture what it shows, so the finding rests on the system and not on a conversation: which account holds both roles, which suppliers it created and whether it approved payments to them, and the bank-detail changes it made. Nobody at Manila reviews the supplier master, so there is no review to read.
rules: Document toxic combinations (segregation-of-duties conflicts) and block them in the role design.
Conflicting duties and conflicting areas of responsibility are segregated. Where they cannot be, a compensating control is recorded: the usual one is an independent review.
What a conflict looks like here
Supplier maintainer lets an account create a supplier and change where it is paid; Payment approver lets it release the payment. One account holding both can set up a supplier and pay it alone.

views.title: Users & roles
views.sub: Finance-system accounts and their roles. Approval limit is the largest payment the account may approve, in PHP. No segregation matrix is configured: the system does not stop two roles being held together.
rows: Group finance, approves the largest payments
Manila IT, runs the finance system

views.title: Roles
rows: Create suppliers and change their details, bank account included
Approve supplier payments up to the account's approval limit
Enter supplier invoices and prepare the payment run
Settings and user accounts of the finance system

views.title: Supplier master
views.sub: Supplier master change log, since 1 July 2026. Reviewed by is blank where nobody reviewed the change.

views.title: Payments
views.sub: Supplier payments, since 1 September 2026, in PHP. Each was within its approver's limit.

parts.title: Who can set up a supplier and pay it
parts.ask: Find every active account that holds both Supplier maintainer and Payment approver, and capture exactly that.
parts.where: Users & roles. Roles says what each role does. Use two filters together: one for the roles, one for the status. Press Capture evidence, then choose the capture here.

parts.title: Suppliers that account created
parts.ask: Find every supplier the account you found created, and capture exactly those changes.
parts.where: Supplier master. A new supplier appears as the change Created. Use two filters together: one for the field, one for who changed it.

parts.title: Was each one paid, and who approved it?
parts.ask: For each supplier creation you captured, decide whether its supplier has been paid since, and by whom.
parts.where: Supplier master gives each change's supplier and date. Payments lists each payment's supplier, approver and date.
options: Paid, approved by the same account

parts.title: Bank-detail changes by that account
parts.ask: Find every bank-detail change the account made, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Supplier master. Use two filters together: one for the field, one for who changed it. Reviewed by shows whether anyone looked.
